title: Al-Khaliq, the Creator
hook: the Creator, who makes from nothing

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Mu'min: the Giver of Safety, and the believer people feel safe around. Your line was the one who makes safe. Who felt a little safer around you? Day two hundred forty-two.

Before a tailor makes a single cut, the cloth is spread on the table. The tailor measures, marks with chalk, measures again. Nothing has been sewn yet, but the coat already exists, in a way, in the measuring. Classical Arabic dictionaries record a word for exactly that moment: khalaqa, to measure out leather or cloth before cutting it. The same word became the Qur'an's word for creating. And the verses tradition counts as the first revelation, the ones we read in camp four, use it twice in two lines: read, in the name of your Lord who created, created the human from a clinging clot. Today: Al-Khaliq, the Creator.
screen: `A TAILOR MEASURING CLOTH.` → `KHALAQA — TO MEASURE OUT.` → `READ, IN THE NAME OF YOUR LORD WHO CREATED.`

segments.voice: The name opens the last verse of al-Hashr. Here is Pickthall: He is Allah, the Creator, the Shaper out of naught, the Fashioner. Three names in a row, and scholars, al-Ghazali among them, read them as three movements. Al-Khaliq, today: the one who determines, measures and plans what will be. Al-Bari', the Shaper out of naught: the one who brings it into being. Al-Musawwir: the one who gives it its form. We'll meet the Fashioner tomorrow. For today, the first movement, and the thing that makes it more than a tailor. A tailor measures cloth that already exists. Muslim theologians teach that Allah creates from nothing at all: no cloth, no table, no chalk. The Qur'an says that when He wills a thing, He only says to it, be, kun, and it is. Kun fa-yakun. And the Qur'an doesn't place creation only at the beginning. It speaks of Allah creating again and again: every birth, every morning, every seed that splits. In this picture, a person didn't just happen once; they are held in being now. Here's a curious detail. The Qur'an sometimes uses the same verb for people. The prophet 'Isa, Jesus, says he shapes a bird from clay, by Allah's permission. And after describing a child forming in the womb, the Qur'an says, blessed is Allah, the best of creators. So people make things too; they measure and shape what's already there. But making from nothing, and holding it in being, Muslim teaching gives to Allah alone. In that view, everything in sight today was made.
screen: `KHALIQ, BARI', MUSAWWIR.` · `THE ONE WHO MEASURES AND PLANS.` · `KUN FA-YAKUN — BE, AND IT IS.` · `THE BEST OF CREATORS.` · then, large: `MADE.`

segments.voice: Take something simple: a sheet of paper, a napkin, a bit of string, a few leaves. Make one small thing with your hands. Fold a boat. Tie a knot. Arrange three stones. Go slowly. Notice how much measuring happens before you do anything: your eyes planning, your fingers testing. Then look at what you made, and at the hands that made it, shaped long before you ever used them. If you pray, you can say, ya Khaliq, softly. The bell holds the time.
Al-Khaliq. The Creator, who measures out and brings into being from nothing, and who keeps creating. Today's word.
Your line: made. Today, pick up three ordinary things, a cup, an apple, your own hand, and say the word to yourself: made. Day two hundred forty-two.

howItsDone: Muslims affirm Allah as al-Khaliq, the Creator of everything from nothing, and reflect on creation as a sign; the name appears in names like Abdul-Khaliq, and the first revealed verses, read in the name of your Lord who created, are widely memorized.

match.prompt: three names, three movements — tap the pairs.

fork.setup: the first revelation begins: read, in the name of your Lord who… what?
fork.reveal: who created, created the human from a clinging clot (96:1–2). in these first verses, the first thing said of the Lord is that He created.

original.note: Arabic: the Creator, from kh-l-q, first to measure out, then to create.

trapdoor: what you thought: God made the world once, long ago.
what it means: the Creator measures, plans and brings into being from nothing, and keeps creating.
what a scholar hears: kh-l-q as taqdir, measuring; al-Ghazali's three movements in 59:24; ahsan al-khaliqin in 23:14; 'Isa's bird in 3:49.

sources.quoted: He is Allah, the Creator, the Shaper out of naught, the Fashioner.

notes: Please confirm Pickthall's wording of the opening of 59:24.
